gap: No result ChatGPT got states the same reviewer's measured efficiency and inverter-on idle draw for the 2 kWh candidates side by side: The Solar Lab got 94% and 9.5 W for the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2, against 79% and about 27 W for the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max and 84% and about 17 W for the DJI Power 2000.
standout_why: Three results were opened. outageoutfitter.com/best/under-1000 (cited, updated 2026-10-19) says "Specs come from the makers; we have not tested these units ourselves" and carries no measured figure. PopSci's Black Friday roundup (cited, 2026-11-26) lists maker capacities and sale prices only. Popular Mechanics (cited) and Business Insider (cited) could not be opened, and the cited EcoFlow sale page was not opened. ChatGPT's answer credits Popular Mechanics with one measurement, 92% of rated capacity for the Elite 200 V2, so a rival has part of this for one unit. Nothing opened, and nothing in either ChatGPT answer, gives idle draw for any unit or a measured efficiency for the DELTA 3 Max, DJI Power 2000, Anker C2000 Gen 2, Anker S2000, Jackery 2000 v2 or Pecron F3000LFP.
decides: It confirms the Elite 200 V2 over the DELTA 3 Max, which ChatGPT picked in its first chat. On The Solar Lab's figures the BLUETTI delivers about 330 Wh more per charge (1,949 vs 1,618 Wh, our arithmetic) and loses about 420 Wh less per day with the inverter left on (228 vs 648 Wh). It also argues for ranking the Elite 200 V2 above the DJI Power 2000 for outage use (94% and 9.5 W against 84% and 17 W), though the DJI's price and 3,000 W output were not read in this angle. The Anker SOLIX S2000 has the lowest idle draw (about 6 W, 91%), but it is a 1,500 W unit on a 7-13 week ship time, so it wins only a long-standby, low-load segment. The Pecron F3000LFP's 37 W idle draw (about 888 Wh a day) offsets part of its 3 kWh advantage in standby use.

findings.label: Measured efficiency (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: Bluetti Elite 200 V2 review - The Solar Lab
findings.note: The Solar Lab calls it "the highest we've ever seen in a portable power station". Load and method are not stated; the page is undated (footer: Copyright 2026). Our arithmetic: 2,073.6 Wh x 0.94 = about 1,949 Wh delivered.

findings.label: Idle draw, inverter on, no load (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: Bluetti Elite 200 V2 review - The Solar Lab
findings.note: The page writes "9.5W per hour". Our arithmetic: 9.5 W x 24 h = 228 Wh a day, about 11% of the 2,073.6 Wh battery. The same review says the unit held a 3,000 W load for over 2 minutes (rated 2,600 W) and recharged from a wall outlet in "just over 1 hour".

findings.label: Energy delivered in a discharge test (StorageReview, Dylan Dougherty)
findings.value: 1.91 kWh out; 2.44 kWh from the wall to recharge
findings.source_title: Portable Power Meets Lab-Grade Reliability: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 Review - StorageReview
findings.note: Published 2025-04-25. The discharge load is not stated. Our arithmetic: 1.91 / 2.0736 = 92% of rated capacity; 1.91 / 2.44 = 78% wall-to-outlet round trip. In a UPS test on a 986-1,100 W server rack, repeated unplugging caused no reboots; no switchover time was measured.

findings.label: Refrigerator runtime on one charge (Bob Vila, Paul Rankin)
findings.source_title: I Powered a Full-Size Fridge for 30 Hours With a Power Station That's Only 1 Cubic Foot - Bob Vila
findings.note: Published 2025-07-17. A full-size refrigerator, model not named. The same test ran a portable AC on max for roughly 6 hours and weighed the unit at 53.3 lb on the tester's scale.

findings.label: Measured efficiency (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max review - The Solar Lab
findings.note: "The efficiency came in at 79%, just shy of earning what we consider to be an 'A' grade." Method not stated; page undated. Our arithmetic: 2,048 Wh x 0.79 = about 1,618 Wh delivered. ChatGPT's 85% assumption (about 1,740 Wh) overstates this unit by about 120 Wh on this figure.

findings.label: Idle draw, inverter on, no load (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max review - The Solar Lab
findings.note: "We calculated the idle consumption at about 27 watts"; calculated, not metered, and The Solar Lab puts standby at about 3 days. Our arithmetic: 27 W x 24 h = 648 Wh a day, about 32% of the battery. The same review timed 0-100% from a wall outlet at 68 minutes and solar at over four hours on the 500 W input.

findings.label: Measured efficiency (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: DJI Power 2000 review - The Solar Lab
findings.note: "An efficiency rating of right around 84%." Method not stated; page undated. Our arithmetic: 2,048 Wh x 0.84 = about 1,720 Wh delivered.

findings.label: Idle draw, inverter on, no load (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: DJI Power 2000 review - The Solar Lab
findings.note: "Consumed right around 17W idling"; The Solar Lab estimates about 5 days of standby. Our arithmetic: 17 W x 24 h = 408 Wh a day, about 20% of the battery. The same review found it "could consistently handle around 3,600W surges" and recharged from the wall in about an hour and a half; it lists the weight as 48.5 lb.

findings.label: Measured efficiency and idle draw (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: about 89%; idle about 18 W with AC outlets on
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 review - The Solar Lab
findings.note: The Solar Lab notes Anker advertises 9 W, which is with the screen and USB only. Page undated. Our arithmetic: 2,048 Wh x 0.89 = about 1,823 Wh; 18 W x 24 h = 432 Wh a day. Wall charge 0-100% in "about 88 minutes"; weight given as 42 lb.

findings.label: Measured efficiency and idle draw (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: 91%; idle about 6 W inverter on (6.1 W in its comparison piece), 2 W inverter off
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX S2000 review - The Solar Lab
findings.note: Page undated. Our arithmetic: 2,010 Wh x 0.91 = about 1,829 Wh; 6 W x 24 h = 144 Wh a day, about 7% of the battery. Wall charge empty to full in about 1 h 47 min. The Solar Lab calculates about 33 hours on a refrigerator using about 1,300 Wh a day (an estimate, not a run).

findings.product: Anker SOLIX S2000 vs EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max
findings.label: Standby time with the inverter on (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: about 13 days (S2000, 6.1 W) vs about 3.1 days (DELTA 3 Max, about 27 W)
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max vs Anker SOLIX S2000 - The Solar Lab
findings.note: The S2000 figure was measured "sitting powered on without running any sort of load"; the DELTA 3 Max figure is calculated "under the same conditions". Page undated.

findings.label: Measured efficiency and idle draw (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: 90%; idle about 17 W; about 5 days of idling
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 2000 V2 review - The Solar Lab
findings.note: Page undated. Our arithmetic: 2,042 Wh x 0.90 = about 1,838 Wh; 17 W x 24 h = 408 Wh a day. It peaked at about 3,100 W for short bursts but did not hold loads above its 2,200 W rating; AC input hovered near 1,300 W unless Emergency Charging Mode was on.

findings.label: Measured efficiency and idle draw (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: 83% at a sustained 3,600 W, full to empty; idle 37 W inverter on, no load
findings.source_title: Pecron F3000LFP review - The Solar Lab
findings.note: Page undated. Our arithmetic: 3,072 Wh x 0.83 = about 2,550 Wh; 37 W x 24 h = 888 Wh a day, about 29% of the battery. A 4,500 W load ran about 10 seconds before tripping; wall charge took just over two hours at 1,800 W; weight given as 63 lb. The review says it launched at $999 and "can usually" be found near $849; that is not a price read today.

findings.label: Who measured, and the limits of the figures
findings.value: All side-by-side efficiency and idle figures come from one reviewer, The Solar Lab
findings.source_title: Power station reviews - The Solar Lab
findings.note: The Solar Lab's reviews quote prices "with our discount code", so it earns from sales. Its pages show no author or publish date, and only the Pecron review states the efficiency test load. Using one reviewer keeps the method consistent across units, but these are single-unit results, not lab-certified.

unsourced: Popular Mechanics' own measurement (ChatGPT says it measured 92% of rated capacity on the Elite 200 V2): the page would not open, so the figure and its method are not verified. StorageReview's 1.91 kWh works out to the same 92%.

Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO and ALLPOWERS R2500 V2: no review of either on the first page of The Solar Lab's index (page 2 not read); no other named reviewer was searched for them.
Measured noise in dB for any candidate: The Solar Lab gives only "quiet"; StorageReview's 16 dB for the Elite 200 V2 is not described as its own measurement.

Measured usable watt-hours for any unit other than the Elite 200 V2: The Solar Lab reports an efficiency percentage, not a watt-hour figure.
Review dates for The Solar Lab's measurements: its pages carry only a 2026 copyright line.
Backup Power Hub's 2,065 Wh at a 200 W load for the Elite 200 V2 and DroneXL's 84% and 29 dB for the DJI Power 2000: seen only in search summaries, pages not opened, so left out.
